chunks: Abu Muhammad al-Muhammadi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Malik, from Ibrahim ibn Banan al-Kha'thami, from Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Amr ibn Thabit, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in a long tradition, who said:

The Mahdi will enter Kufa, and there will be three standards which have become confused among them, so they will become clear to him. He will enter until he comes to the pulpit and preaches, and the people will not know what he is saying due to weeping. This is the statement of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'As if I see the Hasanid and the Husainid who have raised the flags, so he hands it over to the Husainid and they pay allegiance to him.'

Then on the second Friday, the people will say: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, prayer behind you is equivalent to prayer behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), but the mosque does not accommodate us.'

He will say: 'I will survey for you,' so he will go out to al-Ghari and mark a mosque for him with a thousand doors that accommodates the people, covered with tiles. He will send and dig a river from behind the tomb of Husain (peace be upon him) for them that flows to the Ghariyyan until it descends into Najaf. Bridges and mills will be working at its entrance on the path.
And as if I see an old woman with a sack of wheat on her head, until she grinds it in Karbala.

key_terms.أَرْحَاء: Mills, specifically water mills used for grinding grain
key_terms.النَّجَف: Najaf, a holy city in Iraq known for the tomb of Imam Ali (a.s.)
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِيُّ: Descendant of Imam Husain (a.s.), referring to the specific lineage of the Mahdi
key_terms.الْغَرِيِّ: Al-Ghari, a district in Kufa near the tomb of Imam Husain
key_terms.الْكُوفَةَ: Kufa, a major city in Iraq with significant historical and religious importance
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيُّ: The Mahdi, the awaited savior and leader in Shia eschatology
key_terms.الْمِنْبَر: The pulpit, from which religious and political leadership is announced
key_terms.قَنَاطِر: Bridges or structures for water flow

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and events surrounding the Mahdi's entry into Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* details the Mahdi’s entry into Kufa, where he resolves the dispute among three competing factions by transferring authority to the Husainid line, fulfilling the prophetic tradition of the 'two standards.' The text emphasizes both spiritual legitimacy and practical governance, as evidenced by the construction of a massive mosque with a thousand doors and the diversion of a river from Karbala to Najaf, symbolizing the integration of sacred geography with civic infrastructure. This event underscores the Shia belief in the Mahdi’s comprehensive leadership, bridging the gap between the Imamate’s spiritual authority and the material needs of the community.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 485 - It is narrated from Abu Muhammad Muhammadi from Muhammad bin Ali bin Fadhl from his father from Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Malik from Ibrahim bin Banan Khathami from Ahmad bin Yahya bin Motamar from Amr bin Thabit from his father from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) that he said in a long tradition:

“Mahdi will enter Kufa and there will be three standards, which will have become confused. They will be clear to him. He will go in until he comes to the pulpit. Then he will preach, but the people will not understand what he says, because of the wailing. This is the meaning of the statement of the Messenger of Allah (s) that: As if I can see the Hasanids and Husainids that they have raised the flags and each of them are claiming Caliphate. The Hasanid would hand over the flag to the Husainid and all would pay allegiance to him.
Next Friday, the people will ask him to lead them in Friday Prayer.

He will order for a place of prostration to be marked for him with red dye and he will pray there. Then he will order a river to be dug from the rear of the tomb of Imam Husain (a.s), which would flow to the Ghariyyan, so that the water descends into Najaf. At its entrance bridges and mills will be working.
It is as if I could see an old woman with a sack of wheat on her head going to Kerbala to get it milled.
